metadata.title: Nvidia stock hopes to snap seven-day losing streak ahead of earnings

content.text:
00:00 Jared
Worst streaks since October of 2022. Guess what happened back then? We got a bull market. That was the very beginning. Let's go to the Wi-Fi Interactive and I'm going to show you the year-to-date price action in Nvidia. Nice green screen behind us. Let me just pull that up. This is the opposite of what we were seeing yesterday. Yesterday was another red day for semiconductors. But what you might notice here in this year-to-date chart, I'm trying to annotate it. We are just in the middle of a giant trading range. We've gone nowhere in Nvidia for four months. And you might say, well, that's kind of disappointing. But let me show you a comparison of what Nvidia has done versus the socks. That's the chip index. So Nvidia over the last two months is actually up about 7, 8%. Meanwhile, the socks is underwater by 17%, fell into a bare market. So to me, it's impressive that Nvidia has held up. But uh I said this on your show a few days ago, I'm going to be watching for any buyback announcements and, you know, everybody's going to be watching some of the numbers, uh some of the data sender numbers, all of that. I think that's interesting, but uh I'm focused on their investment portfolio. I'm really interested to see what they're how their investments are doing.
01:05 Speaker A
Nvidia's stuck in neutral. Uh, Jessica, what do you think about Nvidia into earnings?
01:10 Jessica
I think Jared hit the point, it's the investment portfolio because what Nvidia has expanded to is really investing in the bottlenecks that are the AI infrastructure. So Nvidia is not only important to the overall market narrative due to the mathematical component that it comprises, but it's also important to the AI narrative because it's going to tell us the demand story. And then of course, they're investing where that demand is. So I want to see that investment portfolio in energy build outs, in those data centers. I want to understand that demand equation and if they're diversifying their revenue with those partnerships, as in renting those data centers outside of just the semiconductors because they are trying to be that one-stop shop for everything artificial intelligence and growing and being agile with artificial intelligence. So I want more confirmation on that, but more to really validate the broader market story and the AI thesis than Nvidia alone. It's uttermost importance.
